title: 1996 AHSME Problem 25
statement: Given that \(x^2+y^2=14x+6y+6,\) what is the largest possible value that \(3x+4y\) can have?

solutions.text: Completing the square gives \[ (x-7)^2+(y-3)^2=64. \] At the center, \(3x+4y=3(7)+4(3)=33.\) Moving \(8\) units in the direction of the vector \((3,4)\) increases the expression by \(8\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=40.\) The maximum is \(73,\) so the correct answer is B.
hints: Complete the square to identify the circle’s center and radius
The maximum of \(3x+4y\) is its value at the center plus the radius times \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}\)
